sections.title: mahouko's starter recipe: name it, describe what shows, then get out of its way
sections.lede: A newcomer asked Tuesday whether there's a tutorial for good prompts and a consistent style. mahouko answered in seven short messages. It's the clearest staff-written V5 starter we've had, so it's now in the guide.
sections.body:
Dokja had just used up the free trial and asked how to write good prompts and keep a style consistent. mahouko's first answer was **Explore**: open an image you like and read how it was prompted. Then came the method, which is worth quoting nearly whole.

**Name it.** "At least tag the character name and copyright (e.g. the show they come from)," using autocomplete or Danbooru's search. **Describe what will be visible, and only that.** "Write absolutely every detail of the character's appearance (hair, clothes, eyes), except for tags which shouldn't be visible due to the pose." Don't describe eyes if she faces away, or shoes if the feet are out of frame. The goal is to **raise the model's confidence**, which is the idea behind most of this week's fixes.

**Quality tags and the UC preset steer style.** Both are on by default. They "improve coherence but do massively steer it towards a common, high-quality style." If you want full control over the style, turn both off. mahouko doesn't specify a style at all. In Studio or over MCP that's a setting, not text to delete: `{"append_quality": false, "append_uc": 0}`.

**Sampling.** Defaults: "like 23-step Euler Ancestral." Guidance "as low as you can get away with. I usually go with 3, but a very specific prompt to give the model confidence." That's lower than the 6.3-6.5 staff figure in the guide. The difference is the very specific prompt that comes with it.

**Two traps.** Put a **location** in the prompt, or "it'll put them on a solid-colour background usually." For more than one character, use **character boxes with positions**: "this will massively improve the model's confidence."

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, Euler Ancestral, 23 steps, guidance 3, normal portrait, `append_quality` false, `append_uc` 0:
`1girl, solo, <name>, <series>, long silver hair, red eyes, black hooded cloak, silver brooch, leather gloves, standing, looking at viewer, cowboy shot, forest, night, moonlight`
Then the same seed with quality tags and Light UC on, then with `forest, night, moonlight` removed.

**CTA.** Three frames, one seed. If the bare version holds together at guidance 3 and the no-location version goes to a flat background, that's the staff claim confirmed. `save_memory` it as `v5_staff_starter_recipe`. Guide: §12 Staff starter recipe.

sections.title: Why 23 is the default, when to use 28, and what Medium is really copying
sections.lede: In the same thread mahouko explained the step count: 23 usually converges, 28 is insurance for uncertain prompts, and Medium is trained to give a 28-step result in 14.
sections.body:
Dokja asked the classic question: does more steps automatically mean a better image? mahouko: **"more steps gives you a more converged image. 23 steps often suffices to give a converged image, that's why it's our default."** The exception: "with some prompts with a lot of uncertainty in certain frequencies, you might feel safer with 28 steps." In practice that means busy scenes, many characters, or prompts that pull in two directions. A clean portrait doesn't need it.

Then on Medium: **"medium-effort is a distilled model which tries to output something similar to a 28-step gen, in only 14 steps."** That matches kurumuz last week ("similar quality to 28 steps at 14"). It also explains why you can't fake Medium by turning High down. Triplis put it plainly: lowering High's steps gives you "the side effects of turning its steps down, rather than the special training of medium." Wemini's verdict after testing: Medium is "equivalent in quality to High at 23 steps, the style can just be sensibly different," and "much better than High at 14 steps in any case."

Staff kept pushing Medium all evening. When people complained about the battery after the boost announcement, kurumuz's answer was "just use medium effort," and "if you don't need UC just use medium honestly." The catch is still UC. Moonbow's prompt "relies a lot on negative emphasis in uc." Ifrit has custom UCs he doesn't want to rebuild as negative weights. Sigurd's point: Heavy UC was trained into Medium, so UC support would need a retrain.

**One lighting anecdote.** He makes zombies finds lighting tags like `dim lighting` "don't apply as much" at 14 steps as at ~19. On High at 14 steps, putting the unwanted lighting in **UC** moved the image more than asking for the wanted lighting.

**Try this.** One seed, normal portrait, guidance 5: High at 23 steps, High at 28, Medium (locked 14):
`1girl, solo, crowded night market, paper lanterns, steam, many people in background, holding a skewer, looking back, dim lighting, high complexity`

**CTA.** If 28 fixes the background crowd and 23 doesn't, that's mahouko's "uncertainty" case. Log Medium against both in `V5 Medium effort testing`. Guide: §7 Steps.

sections.title: Character off-model on V5? Add the series, then describe her
sections.lede: V4.5 recognised many characters from the name alone. V5 often doesn't. The fix this week was the same every time: a copyright tag plus the visible traits.
sections.body:
Givl asked why V5 kept getting Agnea Bristarni wrong when V4.5 was "perfectly on-model every time." ShameSoot's first question: are you using the series tag? His version was `copyright:octopath traveler ii, agnea bristarni, ` and the two gens below came out right. His rule: "with v5 it seems you'll wanna give it a bit more to grasp for a lot of characters rather than just relying on the name," and "every time people have had that issue, series/franchise tags or adding more physical traits tags fixes it." Also: "pls people, do not literally do `1girl, name` as your full prompt and expect gold."

Luca's first check for the same complaint is spelling: "9/10 times I see this complaint the user isn't writing the name properly."

mahouko gave the reason on Monday morning. A character can have "a huge amount of variation in how they're illustrated," and "more data doesn't help with that if the variance remains the same." The cure: "just describe her appearance and it'll fall into the right mode." That's the starter recipe again.

**Outfits without Precise Reference.** He makes zombies: until V5 has PR, the closest thing is "brute forcing as many blue tags as possible," meaning tags that exist on Danbooru (they show blue in autocomplete), to steer to an outfit. His 4 am problem was leggings that stop at the ankle with bare feet. `-3::leggings covering the feet::` didn't work. Luca's fix: `bare feet, ankle-length leggings` and **remove plain `leggings`** from the prompt, because the general tag was pulling in the full version.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5:
`1girl, solo, copyright:<series>, <character name>, <hair colour> hair, <hairstyle>, <eye colour> eyes, <outfit pieces one by one>, standing, full body, <location>`
For the leggings: `bare feet, ankle-length leggings` with no other `leggings` tag.

**CTA.** Pick one character V4.5 knows and V5 doesn't. Same seed: name only, name plus `copyright:`, then name plus copyright plus traits. Post the three. Guide: §8 Community notes Wed 2026-10-14.

sections.title: The Opus Usage Boost: what staff said, and what it's worth
sections.lede: Tuesday evening Anlatan started selling NovelAI's first inventory item: a battery that adds V5 usage on top of the Opus bar. Staff spent two hours answering questions. Here are the answers that matter.
sections.body:
The announcement (Aini, #announcements, 18:37 ET; journal: [Opus Usage Boost](https://journal.novelai.net/novelai-diffusion-v5-opus-usage-boost/), Japanese name 予備電池) is short: if you run out of Opus usage before you run out of ideas, buy a boost and keep generating V5 without waiting for the refill.

**The rules, from staff in #nai-diffusion-discussion:**
- **Your normal usage is spent first** (arda). The boost only fills in after the bar.
- **You need an active Opus subscription** to use one. "Anything V5 that isn't using Anlas needs sub to be active" (catfrog, OccultSage).
- **Boosts expire after about a year**, "I believe" (ght901). Used ones stay in your inventory. luna: "digital landfill."
- **Four boosts cost $24** and give "the same amount of images per month as the subscription" (kurumuz). A boost covers **normal-resolution images**; "it can't do a lot of things anlas can," so large sizes and paid features stay on Anlas.
- No new items are planned (kurumuz), but the inventory system is generic (ght901).

**The numbers.** mahouko says the monthly bar is "about ~7000/month at standard settings. or more if you use the medium-effort model." Wemini priced it out: one boost is $5.99 for about **1,713 images** at 23 steps, while 10,000 Anlas is $13.99 for about 384. finetune checked the two-accounts trick: even timed perfectly, it's still slightly more expensive than one account plus four boosts.

**The free window.** Raezuto's screenshot shows you can type any size. At or under **1024x1024 total pixels** it stays inside the Opus free window. Coded: a larger image, or more than 28 steps, bills Anlas. Moonbow: with several images per request, the first uses the bar and the rest use Anlas.

**House note.** This changes nothing for us. Battery and Anlas spending stays under Yukimi's existing rules, and nobody buys a boost without her OK. For the lab, the advice is the same as staff's: scout on Medium.

**CTA.** Nothing to test. If the Studio battery widget should show boost stock, that's a card for Rook to board. Guide: §7 Opus battery.

sections.title: Lower img2img strength really is cheaper
sections.lede: Monday afternoon a community answer said img2img strength doesn't change the cost. ght901 replied two words: "You are wrong."
sections.body:
mouceen asked whether V5 img2img uses less of the limit at lower denoise strength. TruCubetard said no, only steps matter. Triplis had already watched the Anlas price move with **Strength** at large resolution, and noticed the **Noise** slider doesn't move it.

ght901: **"You are wrong. A lower strength for img2img will use less anlas and less opus limit usage."** Then: **"I'm pretty sure the anlas price is just multiplied by the strength."** That matches luna's September note that img2img drain follows Strength, not Noise. Now we know it's roughly linear.

Kirari~n gave the mental model. Strength 0.6 skips about the first 40% of the schedule. Early steps decide composition and late steps decide detail, so "with very high strength, you can expect changes similar to the change between the first and the last image in that sequence. with 0.5, you can expect similar changes to the change between the middle and the last image." That's why the lowest price you can reach with Strength is below the price of a 1-step gen.

On the Noise slider, Sigurd's verdict: "pretty much useless since v4. either it has little effect at low noise, or it introduces weird noise artifacts at higher noise."

**Try this.** Take any free-size V5 gen and run img2img on the same prompt and seed at Strength 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, Noise 0. Watch the battery or the Anlas readout between runs. Then use 0.5 for touch-ups instead of a full reroll.

**CTA.** If the battery delta doesn't scale with strength, post the numbers in the Cellar. That would contradict ght901. Guide: §7 img2img vs the meter.

excerpts.text: Nah, it uses the same amount of processing power regardless of denoising strength iirc, steps are what matters

excerpts.speaker: Triplis
excerpts.text: notably, changing Noise setting does not change anlas amount with large res - only Strength does

excerpts.speaker: ght901 (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: You are wrong. A lower strength for img2img will use less anlas and less opus limit usage

excerpts.speaker: Kirari~n ☆
excerpts.text: so i2i with strength 0.6 skips over the 40% first steps, and therefore (presumably) saves you the same amount of anlas/usage as reducing your step count by 40%

excerpts.speaker: ght901 (Anlatan)
excerpts.text: I'm pretty sure the anlas price is just multiplied by the strength

sections.title: Why Explore rejected transparent images, what strips your metadata, and the 2^32 seed ceiling
sections.lede: A bug fix on Tuesday led to a useful explanation: NovelAI hides a second copy of the metadata in the alpha channel, and one WebP setting was quietly breaking it.
sections.body:
**The fix.** #changelog, 17:46 ET, luna: "Fixed a bug where `transparent background` image uploads were rejected by NovelAI Explore. The fix only applies to new generations." The cause was a libwebp detail. In lossless mode without `exact`, "RGB values in fully transparent areas ... WILL BE MODIFIED TO IMPROVE COMPRESSION." luna: "if alpha channel is 0 it'll compress the RGB blocks, that breaks nai signatures." Older transparent gens stay unpostable; regenerate them.

**Two copies of the metadata.** 司 PhazonMadness summed it up: NovelAI writes a text chunk (PNG `tEXt`, EXIF for webp) **and** a signature in the alpha channel. ght901: "It's not exactly a usual place to store metadata." Then he explained what removes it:
- **Copying to the clipboard** re-encodes the image "for various, mostly security, reasons," which strips the `tEXt` chunk.
- **Re-encoding as WebP keeps the metadata** "unless you also alter the alpha in some way."
Bicknell125 and Redwood Elf found editors that sometimes keep and sometimes drop it. Teaspoon: browser "save image as" should give you the same file. To share a prompt, share the downloaded file.

**Seeds.** luna: the seed is "`uint64` on backend but no idea what the model does outside of 2^32 range." ght901: the frontend "only will generate up to 2^32." For MCP or API work, keep seeds between 0 and 4294967295.

**Try this.** Generate one `transparent background` image, download it, then copy it from the site into an editor and save it. Read both files with `read_image_metadata`. The download should keep the comment; the clipboard copy shouldn't.

**CTA.** If our Glancewell or gallery export re-encodes with alpha changes, Menma should know. Guide: §7 What strips metadata, Seed range.

For lossless this means 'exact' is disabled. **RGB values in fully transparent areas (that is, areas with alpha values equal to 0) ___WILL BE MODIFIED TO IMPROVE COMPRESSION___. To avoid this, use WebPEncode() and set WebPConfig::exact to 1.**

sections.title: V5 artist weights hit harder: 1.3 is the new 2
sections.lede: Tuesday night #nai-image-advice argued about artist order and weights on V5. The useful part: weights matter more than they did on V4.5, and how much data an artist has outweighs where you put them.
sections.body:
Kalawaki asked how artist mixing changed from V4.5 to V5. Gluttonous Beast: "the weighting now has a bigger impact than before, where **1.3::artist_tag:: has much more value on V5, then 2::artist_tag:: had on V4.5**." Ares keeps every artist at or under 1.5. His method: drop an artist in, lock the seed, and raise the weight "untill i see a major change, or go from like 0.5 to 10.0." Strong artists get lower weights than weak ones.

**Order versus data.** Gluttonous Beast says `artist:name 1, artist:name 2` makes name 1 stronger, "but its also influenced by how much training data each artist has." An artist with much more data wins even when listed second. theincorrigiblemr.p saw that: moving his biggest artist to the end cut his effect. VSEMAN never reorders and says "people get too hung up on the order and don't pay enough attention to more precise weighing." Staff's position (ght901, September) is that there is **no inherent earlier-is-stronger**. So in our guide, tune the weights first and treat order as a minor lever.

**Half-working artists.** If an artist almost works, add tags that are common in their work (theincorrigiblemr.p, Gluttonous Beast). DonationBox's 50-artist test is a caveat: V5 copies simple, flat-colour styles very well but "CANNOT grasp anything beyond the linework" of heavily rendered illustrators.

**Blends you can explain.** Bicknell125's rule: if you'll call a blend your style, every artist in it should be there for a reason you can state. Unlimited Exclusive Kawaiiness builds blends two artists at a time, "so I know what each one adds."

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, one seed: `1girl, solo, upper body, cafe, window light, artist:<a>` at `0.8::`, `1.0::`, `1.3::`, `1.6::`. Then add `artist:<b>` at `1.0::` in front of and then behind `<a>`.

**CTA.** Post the weight strip. If 1.3 already looks like V4.5's 2, that confirms Gluttonous Beast. Guide: §8 Community notes Wed.

excerpts.text: I usually just drop an artist and gen on the same seed incrementing the x.0:: value untill i see a major change, or go from like 0.5 to 10.0, then change from there and yeah some artists are way stronger so I put their emphasis lower than some weaker artists

Putting it like this:
`artist:name 1, artist:name 2` <- name 1 will be stronger
`artist:name 2, artist:name 1` <- name 2 will be stronger

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast
excerpts.text: (Its also influenced by how much training data each artist has too)

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast

If I do artists whose styles are simple, with a tendency towards flat coloring and larger faces, the AI can replicate it very well
If I do like fuggin, Arknights official artists whose training data would be detailed illustrations with dynamic poses, depth of field, shading, etc. the AI CANNOT grasp anything beyond the linework

sections.title: A mole, a haircut, a borrowed hairstyle: when one sentence beats a tag pile
sections.lede: Several small wins this week came from writing the detail as a plain sentence, often in the character box.
sections.body:
**A mole.** patternman: `She has a mole on the right side of her face.` "seems to work well enough. v5 does relatively well for simple directions like this in prose." The exact spot moves around (near the eye, near the mouth), so don't count on precise placement.

**A haircut no tag names.** VSEMAN wanted a very short, side-parted cut with curved bangs. Tags like `pixie cut` or `parted hair` didn't get there. Raezuto's sentence did, in a character box on V5 Full High:
`she has very short side parted, and curtained hair, while her choppy bangs have a pronounced outwards rounded curve that face inward towards her forehead and the back of her hair is cut very short.`
On V4.5 the same sentence needed `0.5::asymmetrical hair::, parted hair, 1.2::side part::` in front. Bicknell125's tip: hair tags work as a set, so try combinations on a locked seed.

**Another character's hairstyle.** Deady The Teddy tried `cosplay` and `wig`. Uragan: "You can prose it just fine in most situations. Tag a character, and prose it to be wearing the other's hair." See the still.

**Tag lookups.** A body pillow is `dakimakura (object)`. `dakimakura (medium)` is the art format (Raezuto, linking the Danbooru wiki). Stirrup leggings are `stirrup legwear` (guestavius).

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 23 steps, guidance 5, one character box:
`girl, short black hair, she has a small mole under her left eye. she wears her hair in a long high ponytail tied with a red cord.`
Base: `1girl, solo, portrait, looking at viewer, garden, daylight`.

**CTA.** Five seeds. Count how often the mole lands under the left eye. If it's 3 or more, `save_memory` it as `v5_prose_small_details`. Guide: §8 Community notes Wed.

excerpts.speaker: patternman
excerpts.text: I haven't experimented much, but something simple like `She has a mole on the right side of her face.` seems to work well enough. v5 does relatively well for simple directions like this in prose, so give it a shot. Of course I don't have a specific location in mind, and the mole jumps around, sometimes close to the eyes, sometimes close to the mouth. So I'm not sure how well it works if you need it at a very specific location.

excerpts.speaker: Raezuto
excerpts.text:
For anyone curious, I did this to get close to that hair style @VSEMAN was aiming for on V5 Full - High Effort (I put it in a character prompt box):
```
She has very short side parted, and curtained hair, while her choppy bangs have a pronounced outwards rounded curve that face inward towards her forehead and the back of her hair is cut very short.
```
On v4.5 it seems the prose *almost* works on it's own, but it needed two tags added in front of it,
```
0.5::asymmetrical hair::, parted hair, 1.2::side part::, She has very short side parted, and curtained hair, while her choppy bangs have a pronounced outwards rounded curve that face inward towards her forehead and the back of her hair is cut very short.
```

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: :V you don't seem to understand how ai tags work then. short hair is longer than pixie cut, and pixie cut is not a super powerful hair shape like bowl cut or whatever so you can manipulate it with the other tags into the hairstyle you're going for

excerpts.speaker: Uragan
excerpts.text: You can prose it just fine in most situations. Tag a character, and prose it to be wearing the other's hair.

excerpts.speaker: Raezuto
excerpts.text:
it's actually `dakimakura (medium)` - that's the Japanese name for body pillow & `dakimakura (object)`
<https://danbooru.donmai.us/wiki_pages/dakimakura_(medium)>

excerpts.speaker: guestavius
excerpts.text: I currently can't check how well NAI does it, but the legwear tag is `stirrup legwear`.

sections.title: A 4koma in one prompt, page by page, and what the pipes really do
sections.lede: Comics came up again. There's no simple comic mode yet (mahouko), but two layouts worked, and Raezuto cleared up the pipe syntax.
sections.body:
mahouko answered the "can it make comics" question honestly: "there are workflows you can use like inpainting, or you can make solo images yourself then compose them together in separate software. ... there's not like a simplified experience around it."

**One prompt, four panels.** Gluttonous Beast's layout "has worked for me all the time." The base prompt names the format and gives one line per panel:
`left-to-right manga, 4koma,` then `view 1: ...`, `view 2: ...`, `view 3: ...`, `view 4: ...`.
Raezuto's variant puts each view in its own **character box** and uses V5's custom positions to place them. Character boxes can hold objects and panels, not just people (Gluttonous Beast).

**Several pages.** Luca: do one 4koma per page and save it, then start page 2 as a new image. "You could maybe use a low-strength img2img to keep it consistent, but primarily consistency will come from your prompt." Low strength is also cheaper now (see the img2img article).

**Pipes.** Kalawaki found docs saying `|` prompt mixing only works on V3 and worried he'd been doing it wrong. Raezuto: on V4.5 and V5, a **single** `|` in the base prompt marks a character prompt without making a box, and `||a|b||` is the **prompt randomizer** ([docs](https://docs.novelai.net/en/image/promptrandomizer)). `cat|frog`-style mixing is V3 only. Redwood Elf's random-portrait image (below) is a randomizer prompt; load its metadata and reroll. ShameSoot's warning: randomizers are an "absolute battery/anlas murderer." Keep them at free sizes on Medium.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, 28 steps (multi-panel), guidance 5, normal portrait:
`left-to-right manga, 4koma, monochrome, view 1: a girl finds a cat on a wall. view 2: she reaches up. view 3: the cat jumps onto her head. view 4: she smiles, cat on head.`
In-image words go in `text_overlays`, one row per bubble, never typed `Text:`.

**CTA.** Compare base-prompt views with box views at custom positions, same seed. Which keeps four clean panels? Guide: §8 Community notes Wed.

excerpts.speaker: mahouko (Anlatan)
excerpts.text:
there are workflows you can use like inpainting, or you can make solo images yourself then compose them together in separate software.
so, an advanced user can do it to an extent, but there's not like a simplified experience around it

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast
excerpts.text:
What I usually do is something like this:
Base prompt:
```left-to-right manga, 4koma,
View 1: first panel description.
View 2: second panel description.
View 3: third panel description.
View 4: fourth panel description.```
Has worked for me all the time

excerpts.speaker: Gluttonous Beast
excerpts.text: Yea, you can basically place anything, objects, animals, manga panels into character prompts, and then position them via the tool as you see fit.

excerpts.speaker: Raezuto
excerpts.text: You can also most likely set those Views they listed within individual Character prompt boxes instead & utilize the really cool custom character positioning V5 has and to make sure stuff appears where it should.

excerpts.speaker: Luca
excerpts.text: Right, so you gen the 4koma from page 1. When complete, you save it and start a new image that is 4koma-page 2

excerpts.speaker: Luca
excerpts.text: You could maybe use a low-strength img2img to keep it consistent, but primarily consistency will come from your prompt.

excerpts.speaker: Kalawaki
excerpts.text: ...Hm. The prompt mixing doc says prompt mixing with `|` is only available on v3 or lower. Is this true? Have I been doing it wrong for months now?

excerpts.speaker: Raezuto
excerpts.text:
with V4.5 & V5 single pipes are to signify character prompt boxes within the base prompt (without making character prompt boxes themselves) & `||these are|for|prompt|randomizers||`
<https://docs.novelai.net/en/image/promptrandomizer>

excerpts.speaker: Redwood Elf
excerpts.text: An example is this "Random character portrait" prompt (Just load the Metadata and it will pick a random character and draw them)

excerpts.speaker: ShameSoot
excerpts.text: endless fun, absolute battery/anlas murderer

sections.title: Negate gently, and what UC can still do that a negative weight can't
sections.lede: The effort-toggle debate kept coming back to UC. Two practical points came out of it.
sections.body:
**Start small.** shambibble: "much like UC, i actually think its generally good practice to neg stuff as minimally as possible, if -0.25::bad thing:: chases it off, probably less disruptive than -1::bad thing::." Ares found the opposite floor on his seeds: below about 0.6 he saw no change either way. So the advice is to step down from -1 on a locked seed and stop at the weakest value that still works.

**What UC still does.** Moonbow: "undesired content can still do the vibes-based nudges that negative emphasis can't. like UCing 'bald' and 'sound effects' can create better scene composition." Sojorn's warning: "UCing certain things can lower quality/introduce weird artifacts." Moonbow: "always test added tags for your intended effect."

**Medium users.** lr80 asked whether UC on Medium is ignored or just weaker. It's ignored: Medium has no UC path (mahouko, last week). Our Studio folds your UC into `-1::` bans in the prompt. Ifrit hopes Medium gets UC; Sigurd points out Heavy UC is trained in, so that would mean a retrain. Ifrit's other point: "some stuff need uc to reign them in as neg is too powerful." When a negative weight is too strong, that's your cue to use High.

**Try this.** High, 23 steps, guidance 5, one seed: `1girl, solo, standing, city street, rain, night, high complexity` plus `-1::umbrella::`, then `-0.5::umbrella::`, then `-0.25::umbrella::`. Then UC `umbrella` with no prompt negative.

**CTA.** Post the four frames with the weakest working weight noted. Guide: §8 Community notes Wed.

excerpts.speaker: shambibble
excerpts.text: much like UC, i actually think its generally good practice to neg stuff as minimally as possible, if -0.25::bad thing:: chases it off, probably less disruptive than -1::bad thing::

excerpts.speaker: Ares
excerpts.text: For me it seemed that anything under 0.6 doesn't do anything, like tests on the same seed but just changing the emphasis either way is like 1 or 0

excerpts.speaker: Moonbow
excerpts.text: undesired content can still do the vibes-based nudges that negative emphasis can't. like UCing "bald" and "sound effects" can create better scene composition

excerpts.speaker: Sojorn
excerpts.text: But the reverse is true where UCing certain things can lower quality/introduce weird artifacts. I just don't really like using it much these days.

excerpts.speaker: Moonbow
excerpts.text: it's a skill issue in that case. always test added tags for your intended effect

sections.title: This week's lab board: the starter recipe, 23 vs 28, weight strips, gentle negatives
sections.lede: Five cheap A/Bs that would turn this week's answers into guide defaults. All free-tier, small sizes, fixed seeds.
sections.body:
1. **Staff starter recipe.** The cloak prompt from the lead, guidance 3, quality tags and UC preset off, vs on, vs no location. Pass: holds together at 3, flat background without a location.
2. **23 vs 28 on a busy scene.** The night-market prompt, High 23 vs 28 vs Medium, two seeds. Does 28 fix the crowd?
3. **V5 weight strip.** One artist at 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.6, then a second artist in front of and behind it.
4. **Gentle negatives.** `-1` / `-0.5` / `-0.25::umbrella::` vs UC `umbrella`, High, one seed.
5. **img2img cost.** Strength 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on one free-size gen; note the battery delta (no paid sizes).

**Settings unless noted:** V5 Full, small portrait, Euler Ancestral, guidance 5, rescale 0, quality tags on, Light UC (High only), HOUSE lowercase, seeds within 32 bits.

**CTA.** Results go in mail to the Cellar plus `save_memory`. Medium rows go in `V5 Medium effort testing` (same name, never a new one), and a lab article goes on this sheet.

sections.title: Behind the red wrapper: even exposure, an animation chunk, 3D renders, and negatives that turn the subject
sections.lede: The unofficial guild was mostly showcase and battery talk. Raezuto shared several reusable chunks, and one outfit thread turned up a general negative-weight trap.
sections.body:
**Even exposure.** Raezuto, critiquing a set: number 1 "needs `-1::underexposure::`." Try it in UC first, then in the base prompt. He also uses `overexposure` and `underexposure` "for images to have even brightness," except when you want dark or bright lighting on purpose. For drama, the opposite: `darker darks & lighter lights, heavy shadows`, and "increasing the weight on all 3 together is fun."

**A V5 animation chunk.** Raezuto's new "Animation" prompt chunk, "primarily for V5":
`very high-quality anime screenshot style, smooth cel-shaded animation with vibrant colors and clean, confident lineart, professional digital art.`
Add `detailed animation` and `cel rendering` (a real Danbooru tag). That pairs with his official-channel anime stack this week: `high complexity, absurdres, detailed animation, anime coloring, anime screenshot, cel rendering, vector trace, clean lineart, -1::white outline, character outer glow, comic::,` on DPM++ 2M, checking Standard vs Light quality tags.

**3D renders.** `copyright:final fantasy vii rebirth, three-dimensional visuals, ultra-detailed, ultra-realistic, ultra complexity, depthness` (Raezuto). The copyright tag sets the render style.

**Negative weights can turn the subject.** matts7123 was fine-tuning an outfit detail with negative weights and found the model "tends to solve the problem by facing the character away from the viewer if facing viewer isn't explicitly tagged." That applies to any front-visible feature you negate: pin `facing viewer` (or the angle you want) first.

**Artist collaboration.** Xan keeps `-3::artist collaboration::` in the base prompt. Raezuto used -4 to -8 on V4.5 and hasn't tested it much on V5. Treat that as a V4.5 habit to retune.

**Channel etiquette** (for anyone posting there): human skin and no snout goes in the regular NSFW channels; anything more animal goes in furry (Whoyo, Gone Postal). For our gens the furry look is still the `dataset_config` toggle, never typed.

**Try this.** V5 Full, High, DPM++ 2M, 23 steps, guidance 5: the animation chunk plus `1girl, solo, rooftop, sunset, wind, looking at viewer`, then add `-1::underexposure::` in UC.

**CTA.** A/B the chunk vs Raezuto's tag stack on the same seed. Guide: §8 Community notes Wed (UNOFFICIAL).
